segments: Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
... they were entering into his presence during the severity of the illness,
the Caliph put his signet-ring on a document (saqra),
and he called a young eunuch and said to him:
"Take this document and go out as if you are playing,
and do not run,
and approach the vizier,
and give it to him."
And when the eunuch took the document and went out as he was commanded,
the physician also lingered a little behind,
and went out ostensibly to pass water,
and reached the ustād-dār in haste and informed him of the matter.
And he immediately sent other eunuchs,
and they went and found the young eunuch carrying the document while still playing.
And they attacked him and brought him to the ustād-dār,
and he searched him and found the document.
And when he took it,
he killed him and threw him into a pit.
And he arose in haste with his companions,
and they entered the inner courtyard of the palace.
And when the maidservants cried out in their faces, saying:
"Dogs,
how did you enter in upon us
as if upon shameless dissolute women?",
they held them in contempt and despised them,
and entered where the Caliph was lying down.
And they said to him:
"The physician has commanded that we bring you into the bathhouse."
And when he grew angry and said:
"I do not want a bathhouse,"
they did not listen to him,
but stripped him by force,
and brought him in and threw him into the inner room.
And when he was being tormented by the heat,
and had no strength to stand,
and was screaming out,
they were clattering at the door,
so that the sound of his screaming might be concealed from the maidservants and the slaves who were there,
because they were not able to drive them away,
lest they be accused of having killed him.
And after some time,
one of the grandees entered and trod on his belly with his foot.
And when he drew near to giving up his spirit,
they brought him out while there was still breath in him,
so that the minor slaves and the maidservants might see that he had not been killed by strangulation.
And when he came out, he asked for water,
and they did not give it to him, saying:
"You will be harmed by water."
Then the physician said to them:
"Give it to him,
because as soon as the water reaches his lips, he will die."
And when they gave him water,
he was unable to suck it,
because his throat had already dried up and contracted,
and in that very hour he died.
